subject: Request: annotated KMS rotation snapshots and access timeline

From: secops@blueharbor.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: auditor@finsight.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: KMS rotation timeline and sample logs for SIG review

Hi Jonas,

We're working through the SIG questionnaire and BlueHarbor's security team has a couple follow-up asks specific to key lifecycle controls. Can you provide the following by EOD PT tomorrow if possible?

- A short, annotated rotation timeline for tenant and service-level keys (last 12 months) that highlights rolling windows and emergency rotations (comments on reason).
- A sampling of KMS/HSM export logs that show operator/agent access events and rotation operations (redact tenant identifiers as appropriate). CSV format preferred.
- The policy excerpt that governs wrapping/KEK handling and how forced-rotation is initiated.

We don't need raw key material — just metadata, timestamps, and verification hashes where available. Finsight (auditor@finsight.com) will use these for validation steps.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Asha Rao
SecOps Lead, BlueHarbor
[Attachment: SIG-ask-summary.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: secops@blueharbor.com, auditor@finsight.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: KMS rotation timeline and sample logs for SIG review

Irene/Marissa — forwarding BlueHarbor's ask. Asha wants an annotated 12-month rotation timeline, log samples (CSV), and the policy excerpt. Can we assemble a minimal package (no key material) that satisfies SIG and SOC2 items: rotation timestamps, operator principal, action type, and checksum/hashes for exported artifacts?

Constraints & notes:
- redact tenant names; provide tenant-id hashes instead.
- include both scheduled rotations and the one emergency rotation in March (brief rationale).
- attach policy excerpt (KEK wrap/unwrap flow) and an export of the access matrix for ops, last 90 days.

Marissa — can you produce the access matrix + operator event extraction? Irene — can you annotate the timeline and pull the KEK policy snippet? I can handle redaction and packaging.

If you need extra time, tell Asha we can deliver a partial set tomorrow and the rest by EOD Tue.

Jonas Weber
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: irene.choi@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 16:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: KMS rotation timeline and sample logs for SIG review

Jonas/Asha/Finsight —

Attached is an initial package for the SIG/SOC2 review. Contents: 1) annotated_key_policy_v1.2.pdf — excerpts of KEK wrapping and forced-rotation procedures with paragraph references; 2) kms_rotation_sample.csv — 24 sample rotation events (timestamp, key_id_hash, rotation_type, operator_principal, reason_code, verification_hash); 3) operator-access-matrix.csv — last 90 days of operators and role mappings.

Key highlights (short):
- Scheduled rotations occur on a 90-day cadence for service KEKs; tenant KEKs are on 180-day cadence unless tenant opts into accelerated rotation.
- Emergency rotation on 2027-03-11 was triggered by a suspected misconfiguration in a third-party router; entry is labelled EMERGENCY_ROTATION with corresponding ticket reference JIRA-OPS-5532.
- All rotations are recorded with SHA256 verification values of rotation manifests; the CSV includes those hashes.

Redaction approach: tenant UUIDs replaced with sha1(id) to allow cross-referencing without exposing PII. Operator principals are listed as role@redwood (e.g., kms-operator@redwood) and an internal mapping file can be produced under NDA if needed.

Attachments: [kms_rotation_sample.csv (text/csv)], [annotated_key_policy_v1.2.pdf (application/pdf)], [operator-access-matrix.csv (text/csv)]

Let me know if you need additional fields (e.g., sequence numbers from HSM attestation) — we can extract but it will take a few hours.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Lead, Crypto Ops
Redwood Inference

Jonas / Irene / Marissa —

Thanks, that package looks good and is exactly what we needed for the SIG checklist spot-check. A couple of quick clarifications from Finsight after a brief pass: 

1) For one or two rotation rows you included a blank "reason_code" (these may be automated housekeeping rotations). Please mark them as HOUSEKEEPING if that's the case.
2) Could you confirm whether the SHA256 verification hashes included are of the rotation manifest only or of the entire export bundle? Which process produced the hash (HSM-provided or post-export compute)?

If you can reply with those clarifications we can close the ticket on our side. No additional files required unless you suggest otherwise.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Asha Rao
SecOps Lead, BlueHarbor
